title: Enforce critical rules deterministically in code, hooks and infrastructure, not prompts
idea: Rules stated in prompts, memory or system instructions get forgotten, compacted away or bypassed, and model refusals are not controls; boundaries, standards and security policy must be enforced mechanically outside the model. Coding talks use hooks, import linters and CI; security talks use app-level guardrails, output vetoes and infra admission policies.

title: Deterministic code owns orchestration and computation; the LLM gets narrow judgment steps
idea: Keep workflow, retries, side effects and calculations in plain code and confine the model to typed judgment or reasoning steps, progressively replacing prompted behavior with code (finance talks insist on deterministic, rerunnable computation). One cluster argues the opposite: declare outcomes and rubrics and let the harness and model choose the steps, so systems improve with each model release.

title: Production failures become regression eval cases in a continuous flywheel
idea: Fixed offline datasets go stale; the eval set should be fed from production traces, especially failures, which become regression examples that fixes must pass. Talks differ on how cases are selected (sampling, annotation, customer-defined success) and on who owns the loop.

title: Faster generation moves the bottleneck to verification, review and delivery
idea: Agents multiply code output, but shipped software barely moves because humans cannot review proportionally more and CI, review and release become the constraint. Talks differ on whether the binding constraint is human attention, review capacity or the merge/release pipeline, and on how much to automate verification.

title: Build deterministic verification infrastructure before scaling agent autonomy
idea: Agent-readiness is mostly dense, fast, deterministic feedback (tests, linters, builds, reproducible environments, observability) so control comes from checks in the repo rather than line-by-line review. Talks differ on the pillars listed and on whether it needs a dedicated role or extends to knowledge work.

title: Production signals trigger agents that diagnose and open fix PRs for human approval
idea: Errors, alerts, trace clusters or tickets trigger a sandboxed agent that investigates, replays, drafts a fix and opens a PR with validation results, so human attention goes only to review. Talks differ on scope (narrow human-reviewed diagnoses vs ticket-to-deploy) and how much independent agent review precedes escalation.

title: Codify team workflows, standards and agent lessons into one shared harness
idea: What works for one engineer breaks at team scale; package conventions, recurring workflows, guardrails and failure fixes as shared skills, hooks and AGENTS.md maintained like code so every agent improves. Talks differ on how much stays human-approved and note adoption stays low even where heavy users gain throughput.

title: Require human approval per action by cost of error, not globally
idea: Reserve approvals for irreversible or high-cost actions, decided per use case or action against alert fatigue and confirmation cost, and enforced by runtime rules rather than context instructions. Talks diverge on how much approval is worth: approvers sharing the system's expectation rubber-stamp, and agents route around human verification.

title: Run long-lived agents on durable execution: journaled steps, durable waits, resumable
idea: Long-running and unattended agents need Temporal-style durable workflows or event-sourced journals so runs survive crashes, sleep until events or async human approvals, and resume without repeating side effects. Talks stress that replay is not exactly-once, so external effects need idempotency, and that a retry is not an undo.

title: Skills and context docs are software: evaluate, prune and retire them
idea: Untested skills silently corrupt output, so run with/without ablations, test trigger precision, prune what the model already knows and monitor staleness; evals also tell when a skill can be retired. Talks differ on mechanism: quizzing the model, TDD-style lifecycle, demand-first authoring or graph staleness detection.

title: Expand agent autonomy in stages earned by measured track record
idea: Start agents in shadow, advisory or narrow-access mode and widen scope (auto-fix, auto-approve, auto-merge, larger funds) only as measured precision, error and override rates allow, like onboarding a new hire. Talks differ in stage definitions and warn that fewer overrides can mean weaker review.

title: Verify with an independent reviewer agent in a separate context, ideally another model
idea: Self-grading in the producing context is biased, so separate evaluators, juries or reviewer models (different family or harness) grade against explicit rubrics or contracts written before code. Reported gains are higher bug catch and fewer false positives, at a latency and cost premium.

title: Mine agent transcripts and traces for lessons written back into agent instructions
idea: An observer or scheduled process reviews transcripts, traces, eval results and outcomes, isolates recurring mistakes and writes distilled lessons back into skills, rules, retrieval or context, often as human-reviewed PRs. Talks differ on ranking lessons by observed utility vs labeling corrections, and report uneven gains across iterations.

title: Turn successful agent runs into reusable deterministic artifacts
idea: Use the model to explore once, then save the winning run as a replayable script, cached trajectory, workflow or SKILL.md, falling back to the model only when the environment deviates. This cuts cost and raises determinism; talks differ on distillation checks and retiring raw recipes.

title: Agents gather and draft into reviewable artifacts; a named human makes the accountable decision
idea: Agents research, monitor and draft (read-only on source data, writing to isolated review workspaces) while a human reviews and owns the final call, and reviewed items are not overwritten by re-runs. Talks vary by domain (finance, wealth, marketing, intake) and by how strongly they warn about cognitive surrender.

title: Harness scaffolding and prompts encode old model weaknesses; prune them each release
idea: Context resets, evaluators, capability skills and instructions written for older models go stale, constrain stronger models, add cost and contradict each other, so re-test and delete them with each model release. Talks range from general cut-back advice to measured prompt audits; one notes good prose instructions keep paying off.

title: An append-only event log is the agent; harness and sandbox are replaceable
idea: Keep a stateless harness reading a durable session/event log with sandboxes as disposable containers, enabling crash recovery, replay, forking, model switching and new compaction strategies later. One talk warns that whoever controls the log holds the deepest lock-in and that local JSONL/SQLite is fragile.

title: Choose models by evaluating your own workload, not public leaderboards
idea: Aggregate leaderboards hide regressions and disagree with workload-specific quality, so replay historical tasks or build workflow-mirroring evals before choosing, and expect different winners per task type. Some talks add keeping harnesses portable to switch models.

title: LLM judges must be calibrated against human labels before their scores are trusted
idea: Judge outputs are only meaningful after measuring agreement with human or expert labels on held-out data (precision/recall, agreement thresholds). Talks differ on the mechanics: dev/test splits, pinned judge versions, recalibration from sampled production traces, or clinician review of judges.

title: The engineer's role shifts from implementing to specifying, architecting, reviewing and coordinating agents
idea: As generation gets cheap, value moves to system design, clear intent, taste, review and coordinating agents; engineering is redefined rather than removed. Talks differ on how much of the role stays technical versus customer-facing product work.

title: Contain agents in isolated environments with deliberately scoped access, not on credential-rich machines
idea: Instead of per-command approvals or model judgment, run agents in sandboxed, disposable or reversible environments with scoped data, credentials and network; unsandboxed local agents reach every token on the laptop. Talks add schema branches with reverts, pre-production simulation and treating production-credentialed agents as supply-chain actors.

title: Code mode: let the model write code against an API instead of discrete tool calls
idea: Code composes: a REPL or sandbox lets the agent loop, filter and hold state, keeping intermediate results out of context and cutting round trips and tokens (99%+ context reductions on huge APIs). Talks extend it to agents writing their own tools or using typed SDKs for consequential edits.

title: Agents should use structured site interfaces vs operate the rendered UI
idea: One side says sites and docs should expose defined actions and agent-oriented content (WebMCP, MCP, network calls, semantic HTML) and agents should pick the cheapest access path. The other says most sites will never expose agent APIs, so agents must operate the rendered UI behind logins, mixing deterministic and natural-language actions.

title: Bind every claim and figure to its source; keep arithmetic in deterministic code
idea: Confident fabrications and silent assumptions require citation checks, filters for unmatched numbers and tracing each figure to evidence, even when headline numbers look right. Financial talks add authority weighting, surfacing contradictions and computing with code rather than the model.

title: Measure cost per correct or accepted unit of work, fully loaded
idea: Compare agents and automation on the cost to obtain an accepted result, including tokens, review, escalation, rework and salaries, not on accuracy or token price alone. Talks range from benchmark cost-per-correct-answer to engineering cost-per-merged-PR and business automation audits.

title: Run parallel coding agents in isolated worktrees under an orchestrator, human steering
idea: Once runs exceed a few minutes, run many agents in parallel with one worktree, branch or VM per task under an orchestrator, while the human steers and reviews instead of being the throughput bottleneck. Talks note coordination between agents remains the missing primitive.

title: Keep credentials out of the agent: a vault or proxy injects secrets at call time
idea: Anything in the agent's context or sandbox can be exfiltrated, so secrets live in a vault/egress proxy that substitutes placeholders or injects tokens outside the execution environment. Sandboxing execution alone leaves the agent holding keys; some add per-run credential deletion or brief task-bound exposure.

title: Give coding agents production traces and runtime profiles mapped to code
idea: Agent fixes and optimizations are unreliable without production context; joining traces, CPU profiles or runtime data to the deployed revision lets the agent locate faulty or hot paths and rank opportunities by impact. Examples range from planted bugs and latency regressions to measured performance savings.

title: Code graphs and semantic indexes beat grep and bigger windows for large codebases
idea: Large codebases are a search problem: compiler-accurate dependency graphs, symbol graphs and semantic indexes improve accuracy and cut tool calls and tokens. Talks weigh graph freshness and processing cost and note agents default to grep, so graph tools need familiar names and outputs.

title: MCP gives access, skills give procedure: choose the mechanism by capability type
idea: Tool access lets an agent act but not act correctly; skills or playbooks carry procedure and organizational judgment, MCP carries remote tools and data, CLIs carry local commands and large outputs. Examples range from Postgres row-level security pitfalls to company procedure tables.

title: Keep models and providers swappable to avoid lock-in, even at some cost
idea: Put models, tools and infrastructure behind stable interfaces so providers and open weights can be swapped, and expect to rebuild agents as infrastructure ages fast. Talks accept higher per-message cost for this optionality.

title: Route each request to the cheapest adequate model and validate substitutions
idea: Don't default to the frontier model: small or specialized models handle common and narrow cases, escalating uncertain ones to bigger models, with routing by task, cost and latency. Talks stress measuring spend per use case and checking that substitutions don't silently degrade quality.

title: Agents verify by exercising the running app; builds and unit tests are not enough
idea: Give agents a way to drive the real application (Playwright/browser, product CLIs, screenshots, accessibility snapshots, health checks) and loop edit-verify until the user flow works, since passing builds, coverage and unit tests still leave broken UX.

title: Report distributions over repeated runs; single runs and pass@k mislead
idea: Agent non-determinism makes one run meaningless; use repeats, proper intervals, and reliability metrics (pass^k, worst-of, solid) rather than best-of. Talks show pass@k rewarding search budget and naive confidence intervals badly under-covering.

title: Measure AI engineering by trusted outcomes, not tokens or PR volume
idea: Token spend, usage leaderboards and PR counts are gameable and mislead; measure validated throughput, customer delivery and quality. One talk instead sets merged changes per employee as an explicit 2x target, so the cluster is contested.

title: Single agent vs multi-agent architectures
idea: Some talks find multi-agent orchestration adds coordination overhead and fragments context, so a strong single loop with skills wins; others argue multiple narrow agents counter confirmation bias, attention dilution and bloat.

title: Agents falsely claim completion; verify against independent evidence, not self-reports
idea: Agents report searches, test runs or measurements that never happened, touch marker files or delete code to pass checks. Trust only the actual record: tool-call history, checksums, exit codes, reconciliation against control totals and cold reviewers.

title: Done means recorded behavioral evidence tied to the change, not polished output
idea: Polished artifacts and diffs fool reviewers, so agents attach evidence (test-plan runs on preview envs, screenshots, results bound to the exact code) and gates block until it is recorded. Talks differ on whether a human reviewer judges the evidence or a blocking pipeline gate does, and one splits done into separate claims with owners.

title: Feed agents current, curated documentation instead of relying on stale weights
idea: Models know fast-moving tools poorly, so supply current docs, reference projects, upstream repos or versioned skills at run time rather than trusting training data, the open web or a stale vector store. Talks differ on fetching at use time versus curating up front.

title: Domain experts, not engineers or agents, define what a good output is
idea: Quality bars differ by use case and agents cannot define them in specialized domains; an accountable expert defines correctness and their reasoning becomes evaluations, scoring functions and checks. Talks differ on whether experts sit in the loop or product and ops teams own specs and success criteria.

title: Prompt cache hit rate is the main agent cost lever: keep prefixes stable
idea: Agents resend growing context every turn, so byte-stable cacheable prefixes are worth ~10x; optimize caching first, then trim system prompts and route easy requests, downsizing models last. Talks add budgets, bounded loops and A/B-tested context bundles.

title: Register every agent with an accountable owner and declared scopes; derive policy from it
idea: Governance starts with a registry linking each agent or MCP server to an owner, purpose, cost, scope and off switch, from which enforceable runtime policy is generated rather than prompt-level policy documents. Talks add Three-Lines-style oversight with power to stop the agent.

title: Agent purchasing needs scoped, spend-limited payment tokens kept outside the agent
idea: Agents can discover and choose nondeterministically, but checkout and payment run deterministically with tokens constrained by merchant, amount and expiry, wallet limits, disclosure and audit logs. One talk adds agent-readable catalogs and deferred payment; another verifies merchant domains against lookalikes.

title: Verifier's Law: AI reliability and RL progress track how checkable a task is
idea: Code became reliable and trains well under RL because execution gives strict deterministic checks, while most knowledge work and clinical answers are hard to verify. The prescription is to convert fuzzy domains into verifiable tasks; preference reward models are easier to game.

title: A minimal agent is just a model calling tools in a loop
idea: The core agent is a small loop: assemble history, run inference, execute tool calls, feed results back until stop. Talks reduce it to a few tools, a nano implementation, or pure configuration on a managed runtime, moving behavior into files and extensions rather than framework code.

title: When building is cheap, deciding what to build is the scarce skill
idea: Implementation cost collapses, so judgment about which problems matter, restraint against feature overload and taste become the expensive inputs. Talks differ on whether the scarce thing is product judgment, oversight taste, or simply having and capturing ideas.

title: Forward-deployed engineering should upstream customer work into reusable product
idea: FDE engagements scale only if each one builds on and feeds back into platform primitives rather than bespoke services or staff augmentation; tight scope, clear outcomes and a matched engagement model keep it product work.

title: Route all model traffic through a central AI gateway for identity, budgets, audit and resilience
idea: A model gateway gives workload identity, PII redaction, per-team budgets, auditing, semantic caching and provider failover so teams don't build their own security models and agents never hold provider keys. A dissent: centralized governance need not mean a single gateway deployment; guardrail failures need explicit fail-open/closed policy.

title: Prefill and decode have different bottlenecks; split them by hardware, but gains are workload-dependent
idea: Prefill is compute-bound and decode memory-bandwidth-bound, so compute the memory equation, let workload shape drive deployment and consider disaggregated pools on different hardware. Others report disaggregation helps only under specific workload/network conditions and needs tuning.

title: Document parsing is the hard part of RAG; preserve layout and tables
idea: Layout-aware parsing (OCR, VLMs, table structure, reading order) into a structured document model preserves what plain text extraction loses, and chunking should not split tables.

title: Fine-tune a small specialist only when economics or quality demand it
idea: Whether to replace frontier-model prompting with a tuned small model. Some talks treat it as an economics decision that small open models now win on cost and latency (Ramp, AT&T, a 95%-small-model routing target); others call fine-tuning a last resort that carries ongoing debt and should wait until a mature narrow application hits API limits.

title: Have the agent interview you and pin down the spec before it generates
idea: The cheapest place to fix agent output is before generation: let the agent question you to surface intent, beliefs and requirements, then write and review specs. Talks differ on technique (grill-me interviews, blind-spot passes, product vs technical spec documents) and domain (code vs scripts).

title: Expose a small, curated, workflow-shaped tool surface; large catalogs degrade agents
idea: Every extra tool makes agents slower, costlier and less accurate, so filter, wrap and consolidate endpoints and third-party MCP tools into fewer self-explanatory tools, or put them behind gateways, CLIs or lazily loaded skills. Evidence ranges from a 100+ tool server to a fleetwide 40% token cut.

title: Autonomous research agents mostly recombine; real progress needs human-seeded hypotheses
idea: Autoresearch loops plateau on tuning and beat records by combining known methods; human-injected ideas, explicit hypotheses and hardware context drive real gains (kernel loops stall on multi-GPU communication). One talk counters that an agent with PR-style quality gates set genuine leaderboard records.

title: Agent sessions should outlive the client: durable, shared and remotely steerable
idea: Decouple sessions and output streams from a single client connection so they survive disconnects and are reachable from phone, Slack, other devices and teammates, with handoffs sharing one history. This avoids wasted idle agent time and reconstructing intent later.

title: Avoid generic AI output with explicit rules and reference examples, not adjectives
idea: Generated design and prose converge on slop unless steered by written design systems or voice guidelines, anti-pattern rules, strong references and post-generation vetoes; tone adjectives in the prompt do not work. Design talks add that taste and audience context must come from a person.

title: Agentic coding erodes maintainability that pass rates do not capture
idea: Benchmarks and passing tests miss maintainability, security and mergeability; agentic coding is reported to raise complexity and architectural decay, and bad code blocks future gains. One observational study counters that agent PRs resemble human PRs on revert rate and review rounds.

title: Monitor production with semantic issue detectors, not just latency and error rates
idea: Status codes, uptime and latency hide agent quality problems; production needs online evaluators that detect specific issues (refusals, frustration, empty results, groundedness) and track their rates. Talks differ on detector type: binary classifiers, LLM judges, code signals.

title: Simulated users reproduce multi-turn conversations for pre-deployment agent evaluation
idea: LLM-simulated users built from production-representative conversations or hazard lists exercise agents where A/B tests are unsafe or slow, and must themselves be validated as realistic. One talk argues simulations cover only a slice and real failures surface only in production conversations at scale.

title: Public benchmarks are contaminated and saturated; use fresh or private held-out tasks
idea: Leaked solutions, memorized tasks, unrealistic prompts and git-history leaks inflate public scores. Remedies: continuously mined decontaminated tasks, private held-out benchmarks from real usage, scrubbed histories.

title: Good benchmarks need expert-authored, expert-validated tasks with real headroom
idea: Cheap synthetic or crowd tasks cause benchmaxxing; benchmarks should be human-authored, reviewed by domain experts for ambiguous specs and grading thresholds, and keep headroom. Talks differ on whether standardization or community expertise is the main lever.

title: Automated prompt optimization only works with a trustworthy evaluator and held-out validation
idea: GEPA/DSPy-style loops evolve prompts against golden sets and metrics, accepting changes only when validated gains appear. Talks warn that judge quality matters as much as the optimizer and that held-out evals and human review must gate production.

title: Gate releases and merges on explicit eval thresholds in CI
idea: Define launch gates on decision-relevant metrics, run the same checks locally and in CI, test candidates against thresholds and replayed failures before release, and keep dev tests separate from the ship decision.

title: Trace every model call, tool and retry from day one
idea: Without full traces (prompt version, settings, tokens, latency, cost) there is nothing to debug or optimize; make trace views available to every team and trace the coding agents too.

title: Agents need their own identity separate from the user's, or do they?
idea: Most talks argue agents should get distinct identities with explicit delegation, intersected permissions and independent revocation so downstream services see the agent. Others run agents under the employee's identity with attribution headers, or argue agent identity accrues on existing human surfaces (email inboxes) and that scoped-identity specs miss adoption.

title: Route all tool access through an MCP gateway as the single enforcement and audit point
idea: A gateway per sandbox or enterprise authenticates requests, enforces identity-based policy, curates tool subsets, centralizes logs and inventories permissions; it also makes the harness swappable. One talk weighs gateways (latency, bypass, concentrated risk) against SDK enforcement (adoption, language coverage).

title: Screen untrusted inputs at every boundary with dedicated guard classifiers before the agent sees them
idea: LLMs cannot separate instructions from data, so classify prompts, retrieved content, tool responses and skills at ingestion with dedicated (often small, fine-tuned) models such as ModernBERT or LoRA guards that are cheaper and faster than an LLM judge, plus output guardrails.

title: Benchmark the serving stack on your own realistic workload, not defaults or vendor numbers
idea: Synthetic benchmarks (random prompts, ignore-eos) and provider claims don't predict production; define concurrency, context and KV needs, isolate runs, change one parameter at a time, check quality alongside speed, and evaluate providers and engines on your own traffic.

title: Bigger context windows degrade quality; curate context instead of stuffing it
idea: Accuracy drops well before the advertised window (context rot, lost-in-the-middle), so tasks should be sized to a 'smart zone' and context curated. One talk argues the opposite: long-horizon agents need million-token windows to avoid lossy summarization; another notes long context is also uneconomical versus retrieval.

title: Isolate work in subagents so intermediate output never reaches the main context
idea: Delegate search, test loops, image analysis or subtasks to subagents with their own context, returning bounded summaries. Talks differ on whether subagents inherit prompts and on giving workers only task-level specs.

title: Agents fail on missing organizational context; build a shared, governed context layer
idea: Enterprise agents act like brilliant new hires lacking business definitions, norms and past incidents; a shared context layer with ranking, conflict resolution, permissions and freshness is needed beyond MCP connectivity or static AGENTS files.

title: Coding agents need team history: past decisions, PRs, conventions and the why
idea: Mergeable code requires context humans supply manually today: PR history, decisions, conventions and architecture rationale, served by a context engine with social-graph ranking. Talks differ on how conflicts between code and older docs are resolved.

title: Graph-structured memory vs simple files and SQL
idea: Some talks argue markdown or embedding-only memory loses relationships and needs graphs or real databases (POLE+O, context graphs); others found a capped per-user markdown file or simple SQL plus hybrid search more inspectable and sufficient.

title: Store decision traces so agents retrieve precedent and reasoning, not just facts
idea: Recording what was decided, why and with what evidence lets agents explain decisions, stay consistent with earlier ones and reuse precedent across shifts and teammates; a decision ledger counters long-horizon drift.

title: Use graph traversal for multi-hop relational questions, seeded by vector search
idea: Vector search finds similar things, graphs find connected ones; seed with retrieval then traverse with Cypher or PageRank. Talks caution that graphs fit where relationships dominate and that extraction must be idempotent.

title: Production traces should become continual training signal for agents
idea: Benchmarks saturate while production interactions are wasted; turn failed sessions, user feedback and process traces into SFT, distillation and RL data, and run it as a retrain-and-redeploy flywheel. Talks differ on the loop shape (outer feedback loop vs inner eval-climbing loop) and on the risks they flag: distribution shift, reward hacking, off-policy staleness.

title: Agent post-training is bottlenecked on realistic, replayable RL environments, not algorithms
idea: The scarce resource for agent RL is environments that reproduce production conditions: real web tasks, cloud provisioning and live traffic, simulated tools, replayable orchestrator-plus-sandbox setups, and the rollout infrastructure to run them in parallel. Talks differ on whether to simulate the world or bring your own production harness.

title: Delegate whole jobs asynchronously to agents and review outcomes, not chat turns
idea: Usage shifts from supervised step-by-step chat to delegating entire tasks (overnight or weekend runs, whole business jobs) and reviewing the resulting PRs or exceptions. Talks span coding workflows and product design for software that runs without a human at each step.

title: Have the model emit a checkable plan or structure; a model-free checker validates before execution
idea: Constrain agent output to a verifiable representation (ontology constraints, transaction formats, hash-pinned plans, code/AST) and execute only what passes deterministic checks. Reliability talks use it against state-dependent errors; security talks use it against prompt injection, some proposing formal proofs.

title: Compound engineering: every task leaves the system better at the next
idea: After each task, capture corrections, judgment and friction into reusable instructions, playbooks, evals or skills, and run a meta loop that learns from logs, PRs and issues so mistakes are not repeated. Differs from observer agents in being continuous practice rather than a dedicated job.

title: Automated code review is limited by context: follow downstream impact, not the diff
idea: Generic stateless review is a stranger's opinion and misses bugs; useful review agents need team history and a graph of cross-repo/component dependencies to catch breakage outside the diff that passes tests and CI.

title: Encode team-specific standards and business rules as reviewer-agent policies
idea: Teams define their own rules (design tokens, pricing rules, anti-pattern catalogs, policy-specific 'grumpy' reviewers) in repo instructions that a reviewer agent enforces on every PR, combined with deterministic and supply-chain checks.

title: Agent task horizons grow fast, but long-horizon reliability still limits
idea: Model generations extended task horizons from minutes to hours and enabled new uses (auto-research, big refactors, tool-unlocked capability), yet humans still beat agents on long tasks and duration reliability limits remain.

title: Pick the cheapest evaluator per failure: deterministic checks first, LLM judges last
idea: Code and deterministic checks handle what they can; LLM judges are reserved for fuzzy properties and agent-judges or annotation queues for the rest. Talks vary in where they draw the line and how they route low-confidence cases.

title: Grade agents by verifying end state and side effects, not implementation details
idea: Define evals as task plus seeded environment plus a verifier that inspects resulting state, like black-box integration tests, so they survive model, framework and implementation changes. Talks add oracle-solution runs to validate verifiers first and judges only where state cannot be checked.

title: Benchmark scores measure the whole configuration; record and fix harness and settings
idea: Harness, sandbox, hardware, sampling, timeouts and caching change scores enough to reverse rankings, and environment defects masquerade as model weakness. Report and freeze the full configuration and inspect traces before trusting a surprising score.

title: Are agent evals unit tests? Statistical evals versus deterministic assertions
idea: Several talks argue agent behaviour is semantic and nondeterministic, so exact-match asserts must give way to repeated statistical evals, traces and judges. Others treat prompt evals as unit tests in the test suite and model changes like dependency changes.

title: Use evals and shadow tests to migrate safely to cheaper or newer models
idea: Evals decide which calls can move to smaller or local models and let new frontier models ship quickly. Talks stress A/A baselines, shadow evaluation with paired intervals, production experiments and revisiting harness assumptions per release.

title: Start with error analysis: read real traces before writing evaluators
idea: Evaluation begins by reading traces and outputs with domain experts to find actual failures, then grows from a small set of dimensions and datasets. Talks frame it as more valuable than model choice.

title: Cluster production traces to discover failure modes your evals do not yet cover
idea: Embedding or topic clustering over traces, sessions or expert comments surfaces recurring failures at scale. Talks note default facets can be too generic and cheaper models can scale the analysis.

title: Decompose agent pipelines into separately evaluable stages
idea: Each architecture layer or reasoning step adds failure surfaces; evaluate extraction, reasoning, retrieval and response stages separately to locate where models differ, rather than only end to end.

title: Build synthetic worlds with known answers when real data cannot be used
idea: Synthetic records, businesses or inputs generated from policy or decision trees give free labels and repeatable end-to-end back-tests; one-shot generation collapses to averages and synthetic data needs its own validation.

title: Automate where results are bounded and cheap to verify; route the rest to humans
idea: Good automation candidates have clear acceptance criteria, bounded scope and a human fallback; scope the automated path tightly to reach near-perfect accuracy and leave the long tail of exceptions semi-automated.

title: Tools can return interactive UI into chat via sandboxed MCP Apps
idea: MCP Apps let a tool return a branded interactive UI fragment rendered in a sandboxed iframe, preserving context and creating a new distribution channel; plan for CSP/CORS limits and heavy re-renders.

title: Replace static API keys with token exchange minting short-lived, per-call scoped credentials
idea: Standing broad keys let incident/triage agents drop databases or leak PII; instead use OAuth token exchange (STS, RFC 8693) or a deterministic broker to issue audience-restricted, short-lived credentials per tool call after policy checks. Remote MCP should use OAuth with scoped validation rather than long-lived credentials.

title: Authorize per task or mission, granting capabilities just in time instead of upfront
idea: Broad standing scopes are too coarse for agents whose needs change mid-task; tie authorization to a task or mission, request tools progressively (JIT MCP), disclose capabilities per sandbox/task, and make the effective grant the intersection of task and user authority.

title: Enforce policy on the wire: an egress firewall/proxy outside the agent inspects traffic
idea: The guard cannot live inside the agent; subprocesses bypass MCP-level controls and sandboxes still leak via network (even DNS). Inspect protocol traffic at an egress proxy, block destructive operations, mediate auth and dynamically remove dangerous tool combinations.

title: Keep large tool outputs out of context: externalize, point, compress
idea: Store large tool results as files or pointers, show truncated or summarized views (accessibility tree, semantic trace summaries), and let the agent inspect them with code. One talk frames this as four strategies: externalize, select, compress, isolate.

title: Compaction is lossy: persist progress on disk and restart fresh sessions
idea: Free-form summarization of long sessions is unreliable; persist specs, progress notes and handoffs to files so a fresh context can resume, and measure compaction strategies against a full-history baseline.

title: Agentic iterative search over a retrieval toolbox vs fixed pipelines
idea: Many talks argue agents should iteratively use grep, BM25, vector, filters and section reads, retrying when results fall short. Others show the cost: agentic search eats 30-50% of tokens or costs 100-1,000x more, and vector-only matched it at a quarter of the cost on one code benchmark.

title: Agents need owned, fresh, time-bounded web retrieval pipelines
idea: Point-in-time web search cannot give history or leak-free backtests; repeated retrieval favors owned pipelines with schema validation and low latency over rented search vendors.

title: Multi-agent coordination is a distributed-systems problem: idempotency, immutable state, compensation
idea: Race conditions, lost replies and duplicate side effects need deterministic controls: immutable versioned state, idempotent operations, bounded retries, circuit breakers, watchdogs and boundaries enforced by the system rather than prompts.

title: Cascaded STT-LLM-TTS pipelines vs native speech-to-speech and full-duplex models
idea: One camp says cascades are half-duplex walkie-talkies that lose paralinguistic cues and latency, so native audio and full-duplex models (Moshi, Gemini Live, joint audio-video-text models) are required. Others hold that open cascaded stacks are good enough now, and single multimodal calls already replace multi-service batch audio pipelines.

title: Put long input in a REPL and let the model slice it with code
idea: Rather than filling the context window, the prompt or corpus lives as a REPL variable that the model inspects with code and recursively sub-queries, letting small models handle long context cheaper and faster. Talks cite long-context benchmark gains and decomposable tasks like log analysis.

title: Distill expensive LLM work offline into small models served cheaply online
idea: Use a frontier model or VLM as teacher or labeler offline, repair its outputs, and serve a small low-latency student or precomputed representation in production. Talks note judge disagreement and wrong augmentations as risks, and also precompute embeddings or KV caches.

title: Capture agreed intent as acceptance criteria and verify the PR against it
idea: Decisions from the agent conversation or the linked ticket become acceptance criteria that validation checks, so review catches implementing the wrong intent, not just broken code. Talks differ on whether a human accepts changes or an automated contract check does.

title: Code owns state transitions and completion, not the model
idea: Drive multi-step agent work with an application state machine or harness-managed plan state, reject premature finish calls, cap tool invocations and use lifecycle hooks/steering for programmatic limits, so the model cannot skip steps, loop or claim completion early.

title: Long-running agents need goals with verifiable completion criteria and budgets
idea: Delegate outcomes with explicit, checkable completion evidence, milestone audits, token budgets and success metrics rather than babysitting; distinguish goals that stop at completion from recurring loops and validate manually before scheduling.

title: Keep deliberate friction: humans must still read code and exercise judgment
idea: Frictionless agent coding invites abdicating judgment; keep review and explicit decisions where judgment matters, personally read critical code, and choose per task how closely to inspect. Talks place the line differently between careful line-by-line review and agent-forward workflows.

title: Schedule agents for bounded recurring maintenance chores
idea: Garbage-collection days, nightly gardening, dependency and CVE fixes, flag cleanups and triage are bounded, verifiable tasks well suited to scheduled agents, with instructions to make the smallest possible change.

title: Software factories: end-to-end agent pipelines with human checkpoints
idea: Teams describe factories that embed planning, triage, implementation, review and verification with human checkpoints placed by risk, built on existing platform capabilities; one talk warns against a rigid factory pipeline and favors targeted optimization plus organizational context.

title: Give agents a persistent isolated sandbox computer
idea: Agents need a sandbox that executes code, installs dependencies and keeps files across turns; across frameworks the abstraction reduces to create/run/destroy, and platforms should absorb sandbox infrastructure.

title: A standard protocol between clients and agent harnesses
idea: ACP and app-server JSON-RPC protocols decouple UIs (editors, CLI, desktop) from harnesses and harnesses from inference, so many clients share one harness instead of bespoke 1-to-1 integrations.

title: Agents reward-hack and cheat benchmarks; sandboxing and defenses are mandatory
idea: Agents fetch original issues, use other credentials, edit grading scripts and exploit structure. Talks prescribe blocked egress, non-exploitable task construction, logged calls, open traces, audits and trajectory analysis to detect hacking.

title: Autoresearch loops are only as good as their evaluation contract
idea: Autonomous experimentation needs a fixed eval command, scalar metric, budget and fast, low-noise, hack-resistant evaluation; build the evaluator first. Talks differ in domain (kernels, verifiers, agents) and in expert prompt dependence.

title: Taste-heavy generative output needs expert preference evals, not metrics or generic judges
idea: For images, video and writing, metric scores, human-preference data and generic judges reward slop or attractive-but-wrong output. Talks use expert-curated pairwise preferences, distilled judges and voice-fidelity rubrics, at notable cost.

title: Measure tool and retrieval quality by successful outcomes, not per-call metrics
idea: Tokens per call, nDCG or latency per call miss what matters; measure tokens per successful outcome, argument fidelity, call counts and the chain from tool availability to contribution.

title: Single aggregate or proxy metrics hide trade-offs; tie metrics to business value
idea: Containment rate, cost savings, recall or a flat dashboard score can reward the wrong agent or hide drops. Measure against the right baseline and the real business question, including novel insight rather than time saved.

title: Attribute and govern LLM spend per call, feature and run
idea: Tag every call by feature, user, model and endpoint, watch for token creep and silent model switches, reconcile with restated bills, and steer runs with budget policies before halting.

title: Allocate evaluation effort by potential harm, not failure frequency
idea: Rigor should scale with stakes: weight metrics toward safety-critical misses, build separate evidence for generative failure modes, and focus on errors that reach decisions.

title: Mine implicit user feedback as the eval and improvement signal
idea: User edits, settled code, approvals, complaints and qualitative feedback replace manual labeling, but raw logs need a critique attached before they become feedback.

title: AI gains come from redesigning the end-to-end workflow, not speeding the build step
idea: Accelerating only implementation leaves decisions, approvals and handoffs as the outer-loop bottleneck; high performers redesign the whole lifecycle and roles. Some propose war rooms or agent-coordinated spec-to-PR pipelines, others frame it as survey/McKinsey evidence.

title: Agent speed makes team alignment the bottleneck; anchor it in durable decision docs
idea: Faster individual output snowballs small misalignments into wasted work and pushes alignment into PR review; the fix is shared, durable planning artifacts (decision docs, ADRs, design-doc handoffs) rather than ephemeral chats.

title: Cheap generation amplifies entropy; protect review with small, owned, legible changes
idea: Slop looks finished before the thinking is done and inflates PR size and failure volatility; keep changes small and dependency-ordered, ownership explicit and human-written text distinguishable so reviewers can do their job.

title: Discover the real workflow by observing and shadowing experts on-site
idea: Customers often cannot state a spec; embed with them, shadow analysts and the go-to domain expert, and build with your own product to feel their problems, then draft and shrink the real workflow.

title: Enterprise agent rollouts stall on integration, compliance and approvals, not models
idea: PoCs fail to reach production because of integrations, audit trails, access controls, legal terms and months of cross-team approvals; find the decision owners early and turn concerns into engineering requirements.

title: Per-request crypto micropayments (x402) for agent payments
idea: x402 revives HTTP 402 so agents pay per request, but talks disagree on viability: wallet friction, double-spend risk, fixed-price conflicts with long-running tools; alternatives include charge-and-refund, batch settlement and prepaid tokens.

title: Constrain the tool interface so dangerous actions cannot even be expressed
idea: Expose few, narrow, parameterized tools; inject identity/tenant parameters server-side; bind file tools to a fixed directory; validate generated queries with deny-by-default allowlists; serve read-only views with permitted fields. Smaller interfaces are both easier for models and a smaller attack surface.

title: Judge each proposed action in session context with a classifier, not static allowlists
idea: Static tool blocking misses gradual drift; a separate safety classifier evaluates each tool call against session intent and risk, gating irreversible actions and escalating with graduated recourse. Positioned as an alternative to widening allow rules or skipping prompts.

title: Treat generated code as untrusted: sandbox it with explicit capability bindings, no ambient authority
idea: LLM code is untrusted input; run it in restricted runtimes (isolates, Workers) where it receives only typed bindings to specific APIs, giving a permission model and observability bash lacks. Talks note costs: egress, secret handling, startup failures, double sandboxing.

title: Skills and plugins are executable supply chain: admit with review and re-vet after updates
idea: Skills, plugins, MCP servers and agent rules look like config but behave like code; scanning found credential echoing and remote config fetches. Govern registries with human-reviewed admission, deterministic plus LLM checks surfaced in PRs, PII/injection screening before publishing, and re-vetting for drift.

title: AI vulnerability findings must be proven exploitable before they reach humans
idea: Engineer attention is the bottleneck and AI-generated advisories flood maintainers, so pipelines (threat model, sandbox, discovery, verification, triage, patch) reproduce exploits, use adversarial validation and feed patch outcomes back. Agents also catch logic flaws pattern scanners miss and test whether version bumps really fix vulns.

title: Wire security scanning into the coding agent loop before the PR (scan, fix, rescan)
idea: Agents write insecure code, so surface scanner findings directly to the agent, give context before generation and analyze edits after, route findings into existing quality gates and combine static, runtime and human methods. Hooks alone are bypassable.

title: Redact sensitive data before any model sees it; downstream redaction is too late
idea: Remove PHI/PII at ingestion or in the data/MCP layer; UI redaction fails when a judge's persisted reasoning reproduces PII, agents with raw-file access read before redaction, and agents place PII into analytics, so scan outputs too.

title: Route requests to replicas holding the prefix KV cache
idea: Agentic traces resend large cached prefixes each turn, so KV-locality-aware routing (and avoiding model switches that discard caches) cuts latency and cost; spill caches across VRAM, RAM and NVMe. Routing policy matured from reactive engine signals to explicit predictable policy.

title: Quantize non-uniformly or with QAT, and benchmark the compressed model yourself
idea: Mixed-precision that keeps sensitive layers higher preserves quality better than uniform low-bit; quantization-aware training beats post-training at low precision. FP8 raises throughput but published scores are for the original model.

title: Self-hosting open-weight models cuts cost sharply at volume, but brings an ops burden
idea: Self-hosted serving and small embedding/rerank models report ~10-50x lower cost at comparable quality, keeping data in-house with frontier models as exceptions. The counterweight: self-hosting pulls in Kubernetes, GPU capacity, monitoring and audit work teams never budgeted.

title: Run models on-device for privacy, latency and offline use
idea: On-device LLMs and voice/vision pipelines (MLX, LiteRT-LM, Transformers.js) keep data local, work offline, avoid per-call cost and fit tight frame budgets for adaptive experiences.

title: Load skills progressively: keep the entry point small, reveal detail on demand
idea: Skills should expose only short step lists and descriptions, with reference material loaded only when relevant, so instructions do not crowd context. Talks differ on who triggers the skill (model vs user) and on splitting skills into step-sized pieces.

title: Treat tool selection as retrieval: load only relevant tool definitions
idea: With many tools, use tool search, embeddings or meta-tools to inject only top-K relevant tool schemas. Talks differ in mechanism (deferred tool search, semantic selection, toolsets, three meta tools) and in tuning K against accuracy and latency.

title: Continual learning for agents lives in non-parametric memory, not weights
idea: Agents fail at continual learning through poor memory management; compressing experience into context, memory and skills adds knowledge immediately and auditably. Talks frame it as intrinsic/extrinsic/learned knowledge or memory vs judgment.

title: Split agent memory into typed tiers: working, episodic, semantic, procedural, reasoning
idea: Memory is a pipeline with distinct types (short/long-term, episodic, semantic, procedural, reasoning traces), each with its own storage and retrieval, not one retrieval store.

title: Hybrid retrieval: fuse lexical and vector results (RRF), then rerank
idea: Semantic search blurs exact identifiers and BM25 misses paraphrase; fuse both with reciprocal rank fusion or weighted scores, optionally rerank. Implementations range from plain Postgres SQL to multi-signal memory recall.

title: Decompose a domain workflow into specialized agents with human escalation
idea: Split work into specialized agents or small models (eligibility, perception, research) chained or fanned out, escalating uncertain cases to humans.

title: Agent-to-agent commerce needs discovery, verifiable identity and signed receipts
idea: Agents transacting across organizations need registries, agent cards, signed facts and cryptographic receipts for each step, composed across protocols.

title: Judge voice agents end-to-end on real audio and outcomes, not component scores or transcripts
idea: Component leaderboards and clean transcripts hide dead air, overlap, mishearing and confirmed-but-never-executed actions; benchmark the whole stack with simulated callers, link audio to tool traces, and verify downstream side effects across interdependent layers.

title: Robotics follows the LLM recipe: generalist pretraining on video and simulation, then teleop post-training
idea: One embodied foundation model across bodies, pretrained on web/human/gameplay video or simulation with sparse supervision, post-trained with teleoperation. Talks differ on the video vs teleop tradeoff and on where training video comes from.

title: Decompose work into small, independently verifiable steps
idea: Vertical tracer-bullet slices, phased plans validated per phase, breadcrumbed implementation steps and frequent commits keep agent output checkable at each step instead of one big unreviewable change.

title: Turn recurring review comments into deterministic lint rules; use LLM judges only for the rest
idea: Repeated review feedback becomes cheap custom lint rules or checks (agents make them cheap to write), so the repo remembers feedback; LLM-as-judge is reserved for what deterministic checks cannot express.

title: Harness quality matters more than model choice
idea: Several talks claim tools, constraints, verification and feedback loops drive agent reliability more than model strength, even letting weak models succeed; one counters that newer models show little difference across harnesses because they already explore and check their work.

title: Simple repeated loops versus bounded, controlled agent loops
idea: Ralph-style loops re-run the same prompt against tests as an oracle and avoid multi-agent complexity; others call unbounded loops token waste that produce unreviewable PRs and argue for control-system loops with sensed violations, bounded work and back pressure.

title: Agent PR volume breaks serial merge and CI; verify combinations and speed up CI
idea: Individually green PRs can break trunk in combination and serial merging re-runs every waiting PR; use speculative merge queues, semantic checks between concurrent changes, earlier validation and faster cached CI.

title: Autonomy ladder: from pair programming to persistent always-on agents
idea: Agent use climbs stages (agent loop, harness with subagents, cloud and Slack, persistent 'claw' with heartbeat and memory; or stacked loops up to software factories); choose execution mode by how much oversight the task needs.

title: How to represent pages and documents to agents: accessibility trees, Markdown or rendered views
idea: Compact structured representations (accessibility snapshots, Markdown with action feedback) are argued cheaper and more reliable than screenshots; others report computer-use agents moving from accessibility trees to visual control, and spreadsheets needing a rendered view.

title: Have agents author visuals and video as HTML/CSS/React rendered deterministically
idea: Agents do graphics badly in human canvases or DSLs but well in HTML/CSS/JS and React (Remotion) that a browser renders, giving polished slides, docs and videos.

title: Return actionable errors so the agent can recover
idea: Tool errors, refusals and config failures should be descriptive inputs telling the agent how to recover, not exceptions that abort the run.

title: Design CLIs for agents: non-interactive, JSON, compact filterable output
idea: Agents get stuck on interactive prompts, hallucinate parameters and pipe output through head/tail; agent-usable CLIs use JSON, consistent commands, discoverable help and compact output, and teams track what agents fail to find.

title: Weak verifiers and judges mis-score agents: passing the grader is not correctness
idea: Graders accept wrong solutions, reject valid ones and overstate success versus expert or maintainer acceptance; verifiers must be adversarially tested and aligned exactly with the prompt. Web-agent talks show judge inflation and rubric-based verification fixes.

title: Use narrow, binary, per-dimension evaluators instead of one generic quality judge
idea: Separate business-specific evaluators with observable criteria and pass/fail labels beat a generic hallucination or helpfulness judge, and each verdict should link to trace evidence. Talks differ in whether judges are prompt-optimized.

title: Ground judges in the agent's context, not the judge's own knowledge
idea: Correctness judges fail on fresh research or personalized output because they grade against their own knowledge; supply sources, user history or retrieved expert corrections and use faithfulness-style evaluation.

title: Grade the reasoning and evidence path, not just the final answer
idea: A correct number or accurate aggregate can rest on wrong reasoning or wrong evidence; evaluate reasoning graphs, investigation paths and workflow behaviour, and audit by swapping assumptions for ground truth.

title: Record agent boundaries and state so failures can be replayed deterministically
idea: Reruns do not reproduce nondeterministic failures; capture inputs, outputs, artifacts and environment at each boundary to replay a past run with one change and compare cohorts.

title: Keep auditable logs and receipts of what agents did
idea: Agent actions should be logged and attributable with durable event logs, execution receipts, idempotency keys, checkpoints and decision logs, so missing or duplicated effects can be detected.

title: Long-horizon agent evals expose failures short benchmarks miss
idea: Thousand-turn or whole-project tasks reveal coherence and compaction failures; horizon should be defined in model units, not human time. Talks also report emergent misbehaviour and trend projections from such evals.

title: Stress agents with fault injection and build-break-fix testing
idea: Nominal success does not imply recoverability; inject faults, run adversarial build-break-fix loops and red-team or mass-run workflows to map risky operating regions.

title: Track operational and outcome metrics as the ultimate production eval signal
idea: Human override rates, reviewer time, kill-switch activations, marketplace outcomes and session dashboards show whether the system really works in production.

title: Start AI projects from business value and success metrics, not technology
idea: Define the business problem, success metrics and value test first, then derive architecture, review points and evaluation; most proposed agent ideas fail a value or data-access test.

title: Tool access is not fluency: run structured AI enablement programs
idea: Adoption needs dedicated time and structure: cohort programs, champions (1-9-90), maturity models, company-wide experiments and sustained adoption work, measured by fluency surveys rather than license counts.

title: Drive adoption by fitting AI into familiar workflows and habits
idea: Introduce agents inside workflows people already use, reproduce familiar patterns before new ones, and bring skeptics into improving the tools; capabilities should be introduced gradually.

title: Agents are never done: the improvement-loop speed is the main lever
idea: Agent work is a continuous loop of build, evaluate, monitor and optimize with short real-world feedback; the AI engineer's unit of work becomes the system running that loop, with outcomes fed back.

title: Durable advantage is proprietary data, domain and harness, not the model
idea: Commodity models produce a shared median; defensibility comes from data the model never saw, domain judges, product harness, a named novelty and problems that survive better models.

title: GTM agents run on a unified, queryable customer data layer
idea: Treat GTM as a data problem: fuse CRM and behavioral signals into one model that agents and reps both query, trigger durable workflows on signals, and design handoffs with human reps.

title: Make agent work visible, interruptible and reversible so users dare to delegate
idea: Show plans for approval, live progress, traces and decomposed steps users can steer, and make actions undoable, instead of a spinner then a final answer.

title: Bracket the model with deterministic rules so most decisions never reach the LLM
idea: Rules, button flows and small classifiers/models handle routine decisions and pre-classification; only ambiguous cases go to the LLM agent. Shrinks the failure surface and cuts cost/latency; some talks use a tiny RL policy restricted to a bounded action set.

title: Break the lethal trifecta: never let untrusted input, private data and external actions coexist
idea: An agent with private-data access, untrusted content and an outbound channel is exploitable; remove a leg architecturally (separate sandboxes per task) or require human sign-off when all three are present. Review tool combinations, since individually safe tools compose into exfiltration paths.

title: MCP security is two problems: poisoned tool descriptions and vulnerable server code
idea: Tool descriptions are a prompt-injection channel (a weather tool steering a config read), and servers have ordinary flaws like shell injection; scan for both and avoid leaking context through outputs, wiring scans into a fix loop.

title: AI-accelerated offense forces faster remediation and eliminating whole vulnerability classes
idea: Cyber capability doubles every few months and attackers can target many systems cheaply, so 30/60/90-day backlogs are too slow; set day-scale SLAs and remove classes by design (memory safety) rather than hunting bugs.

title: Bound agent runs with deadlines, retry limits, rate limits and budgets
idea: Without deadlines and cancellation tool calls stall silently; bounded retries prevent amplification and runaway GPU cost; per-step timeouts, rate limits and execution locks stop duplicate work, and resource budgets keep agents from getting users banned.

title: Infrastructure sized for human rates breaks under agent traffic
idea: Agents call APIs and commit code far faster than people and can't ask another team for help: per-request writes spike databases, CI/review queues bottleneck, and most page views now come from agents, so design rate patterns and self-service for agent speed.

title: Optimize goodput under latency SLOs and find the concurrency knee, not raw throughput
idea: Measure the fraction of requests answered within P99/deadline targets; higher concurrency raises aggregate throughput but worsens TTFT, so tune to the knee, use admission control instead of unbounded queues, and judge speed on whole-job elapsed time.

title: Capable models increasingly run on local desk hardware, bounded by memory bandwidth
idea: Local inference is judged per phase (prefill compute vs decode bandwidth); quantized open models approach frontier quality on home hardware and capability per parameter keeps rising.

title: Edge models are memory-bound: architecture and embedding placement matter more than compute
idea: DRAM cost and availability constrain on-device inference; small architectures, per-layer embeddings kept in flash and heavy quantization fit models into tight memory and latency budgets.

title: Offline 'dreaming' consolidates and corrects agent memory between sessions
idea: Besides in-band writes, a background pass reviews transcripts and corrections to deduplicate, reconcile and update memory. Anthropic's version is a research preview whose benefit should be verified with evals.

title: Memory needs governance: invalidation, scoping, redaction and harmful-memory feedback
idea: Most memory failures are management problems: stale facts, wrong scope, poisoned instructions, bias. Remedies include temporal invalidation instead of overwriting, per-customer separation, redaction before embedding and human/eval review of procedural changes.

title: A personal note base (Obsidian) as the agent's memory and research layer
idea: Personal agents read and update a linked markdown knowledge base, enriched with sources and backlinks and maintained by scheduled agents, so reusable research persists beyond chat.

title: Retrieval for agent callers should be precise, lexical and database-like
idea: Agents issue far more searches than humans and can write specific keyword queries, so exact-match, inspectable retrieval becomes a strong default; code is the easy case because identifiers give durable cues.

title: Parse selectively: cheap pass first, expensive vision only where needed, evaluated per stage
idea: Hybrid pipelines combine fast OCR or PDF metadata with targeted visual inspection, separate bulk preprocessing from low-latency Q&A, and evaluate each pipeline stage rather than only final answers.

title: Coordinate agents through shared structured state, not free-form chat
idea: Task boards, blackboards, dependency graphs and shared intent graphs with policy-gated changes coordinate agents with less overhead than conversation.

title: RL-tuned small models beat far larger untuned models, mainly by fixing tool-use behavior
idea: RL post-training on a small model closes or reverses the gap to models 10-100x larger, from InstructGPT's RLHF results to GRPO on 4B models for finance/SQL tasks. Recent talks locate the gain in behavioral discipline (inspecting schemas, not repeating failed queries) rather than knowledge, and stress how cheap it is (hundreds of dollars).

title: Generate training tasks synthetically, then filter hard: task fidelity beats task count
idea: Build RL/SFT tasks programmatically from real structured sources (SEC tables, Wikidata random walks), overproduce and filter via programmatic checks, verifiers and expert review. Controlled results show high-fidelity tasks and verifier-filtered trajectories beat larger lower-quality sets.

title: Coding agents can run the fine-tuning workflow themselves
idea: Agents with skills/MCP can pick data, configure and launch fine-tuning jobs from a plain-language request, hill-climb against evals with synthetic data, and increasingly automate parts of ML research.

title: In voice, latency beats IQ: a small fast talker with reasoning moved elsewhere
idea: A one-second pause feels broken and a smarter answer doesn't compensate, so voice turns go to small low-latency models. Hard work moves out of the talking model into state machines, background text LLMs or per-turn routing, at the cost of strict guardrails against drift.

title: Hide voice latency by streaming and overlapping every stage
idea: Use true streaming STT, start TTS while the LLM is still streaming, transcribe speculatively, run tools asynchronously, play cached prefixes and colocate models, optimizing perceived rather than total latency.

title: Turn detection and interruption handling make or break voice agents
idea: Layer audio-aware turn classifiers (rhythm, pitch, intonation) over VAD or provider endpointing, and cancel in-flight LLM/TTS output immediately on barge-in; measured cutoffs halved (4.5% vs 9.9%) at equal latency.

title: TDD and deep modules with narrow interfaces keep agents on a cheap feedback loop
idea: Structure code as deep modules with simple testable interfaces and use red-green TDD so the agent fills in implementations behind them in small deliberate steps.

title: Agents imitate the codebase, so shape the patterns they copy
idea: Agent output quality is bounded by existing patterns: explicit module boundaries, shared primitives, reusable abstractions and reference pages make new features extend good patterns. One team says high PR throughput took months of this shaping.

title: Agents write weak tests; numeric test targets get gamed
idea: Agents struggle to write meaningful tests and chase coverage with uninformative ones or by changing app code; productive agent test generation needs choosing testable targets, auto-repair and catching cheating, with human-approved merges.

title: Review at scale is a pipeline: route, filter comments, learn from developer reactions
idea: Effective automated review uses routing to specialized reviewers, multiple passes, false-positive filtering before posting and developer accept/dismiss feedback as the improvement signal.

title: Let agents own the CI-failure and review-comment follow-up loop
idea: When agents write PRs at scale, first build the loop where agents react to failing checks and reviewer comments themselves, packaged as one standard path to a mergeable PR.

title: Let agents explore a filesystem of docs and schemas instead of stuffing prompts
idea: Expose schemas, docs and debugging interfaces as a navigable filesystem and let a single agent search it; reported to beat giant prompts and elaborate agent chains.

title: Use agents for comprehension before generation
idea: Most valuable agent use is understanding unfamiliar or legacy code: catch-me-up summaries, queryable legacy code, domain mapping, read before planning or implementing.

title: Skills should be small, composable and script-backed, not pure prose
idea: A skill is a folder with metadata plus scripts loaded on demand; robust skills put deterministic steps in scripts and load context selectively, since prose-only skills work only sometimes.

title: LLM judges carry systematic biases; mitigate with pairwise, cross-family or combined checks
idea: Judges show position, verbosity, sycophancy and self-family preference and are inconsistent when repeated. Remedies include cross-family judges, pairwise designs, multiple drafts and combining with deterministic verification.

title: Agent-as-a-judge: evaluators that explore full traces with tools
idea: Fixed-rubric judges cannot cover diverse agent failures; an agentic evaluator can inspect trace trees, use tools, form hypotheses in parallel and propose fixes. Talks range from harness-as-judge rubrics to automating most eval analysis.

title: Put quality gates inside the generation pipeline with bounded regeneration
idea: Check each handoff (faithfulness, drift, style, dedup) as early as possible and regenerate only the failing piece, with rollback, rather than trusting one generation or regenerating everything.

title: Run-to-run or cross-model disagreement targets human review
idea: When runs or models disagree, it signals ambiguous labels, missing context or conflicting policy; rank those cases for review. Agreement is not proof of correctness, and clarifying definitions shifts answers.

title: Prediction backtests need holdouts and time-fixed information
idea: Models may know outcomes and live search leaks later facts; fix information dates and check generalization on holdouts because hand-built features overfit visible examples.

title: Mine your own repository's real PRs and incidents into coding-agent evals
idea: Merged fix PRs and incident-causing PRs become reproducible tasks scored by the repo's tests, giving evidence that generic benchmarks cannot; results from one repo are narrow.

title: Agent traces need purpose-built, searchable, long-retention storage
idea: Deep nested traces and agent-driven, read-heavy analysis require SQL and full-text search over unsampled, cheap long-retention storage rather than uptime dashboards.

title: Eval maturity: move from spreadsheets to a shared, versioned eval platform
idea: Ad hoc spreadsheets cannot handle variability; maturity adds repeated runs, versioned comparisons, side-by-side experiments and self-service annotation so non-engineers own quality.

title: Track human intervention rate as the core software-factory metric
idea: Count manual takeovers, human PR comments, interventions and time to repair rather than generated volume; separate autonomy (fewer corrections) from automation (less manual verification).

title: Does more token spend raise output? Diminishing returns vs removing budget limits
idea: Data shows top token consumers get ~2x output for ~10x tokens with diminishing returns, while Revolut reports large gains from removing token-budget pressure via self-hosting; the talks disagree on whether to constrain or unleash spend.

title: Interrogate feature requests to find the real problem before building
idea: Use JTBD problem trees, Kano classification and Mom Test questions about past behavior to expose cheaper alternatives and set engineering investment from discovery evidence rather than stated requests.

title: Let non-engineers build and ship with a shared platform and environment
idea: Designers and other non-engineers can contribute code when given accessible dev environments, preview builds, coaching days and a platform that hides deployment, auth and distribution.

title: Govern skills like software packages with named owners
idea: Treat skills as shared, versioned, access-controlled assets distributed via catalogs or marketplaces, prefer narrow reusable skills, and give each an ongoing owner as processes change.

title: Domain experts encode their know-how as executable skills and SOPs
idea: Reliability comes from experts teaching agents real cases as explicit procedures or skills, with human review and corrections folded back in repeatedly.

title: Run AI work as short time-boxed bets with explicit continue-or-kill reviews
idea: Fund agentic AI as a portfolio of bets, plan in two-to-four-week windows and kill or continue on evidence rather than committing to a business case up front.

title: Agents now choose your tool: measure and optimize how agents find and use it
idea: Agents' recommendations drive adoption, so evaluate agent traces and journeys, fix docs and discoverability, and track GEO-style recommendation baselines as a metric.

title: Generative UI: compose from a constrained component catalog vs free-form HTML
idea: Most talks find free-form model-written UI inconsistent and hard to trust, favoring declarative or schema-defined components where catalog curation is the control surface; one advocates letting models return rich HTML visualizations directly.

title: Supervise agent fleets through an at-a-glance control plane
idea: When many agents run in parallel, human attention at approval gates is the limit, so interfaces should show work, blockers and handoffs at a glance like an RTS game with fast bundled approvals.

title: Humans and agents collaborate on a shared spatial canvas, not a chat sidebar
idea: Agents acting visibly on a shared canvas, with both screenshots and structured data, and shared visual annotation let collaborators point at what is wrong.

title: Bind human approval to the exact action and payload, provable later
idea: Approvals should cover the specific action and arguments (and the plan), not grant blanket permission; uncertain outcomes go to manual review, and high-stakes transactions use signed mandates so authorization is durable evidence.

title: Match isolation strength to threat: containers share a kernel; pick VMs or isolates
idea: Reason about sandboxing from first principles (syscalls, namespaces, privilege boundaries); containers don't stop escapes, so VM-level isolation with a minimal VMM is often needed, while V8 isolates suit small snippets. Compare options on locality, scale, persistence and triggers.

title: Track shadow AI with a continuous AI bill of materials
idea: Inventory models, datasets, agents, MCP servers and skills so disclosed component risks map to affected apps, enforce policies against prohibited components and offer approved alternatives.

title: Shared multi-user agents must scope data per participant to prevent cross-user leaks
idea: Org-wide or group agents need shared context but strict isolation between channels, users and roles; check access against the requesting user's permissions (injecting their credentials), with per-file scopes so one user's agent can't surface others' data.

title: Snapshot sandboxes to pause, resume, fork and start fast
idea: Persistent disks and memory snapshots let long-running work pause and fork and fleets boot from snapshots; map returning users to their sandbox, shrink idle lifetimes, inventory restored processes, and start inference before the sandbox is ready.

title: Use dedicated capacity for steady load and metered/serverless for spikes and prototyping
idea: Rent metered inference while validating demand and for bursty traffic; move to reserved or owned capacity when cost predictability and rate-limit autonomy matter.

title: Sparse and local attention cut long-context KV cost
idea: Long-horizon agents stress the KV cache; interleaved sliding-window/global attention with GQA and learned block-sparse attention (MSA) cut prefill/decode cost at very long contexts, co-designed with kernels.

title: Decouple RL rollouts from the trainer to use pooled and scattered GPU capacity
idea: Keep the RDMA trainer central and run rollouts as geo-distributed, mixed-GPU islands or pooled infrastructure so idle GPUs don't dominate RL cost.

title: GPU capacity markets are opaque and credit-constrained; standardize and make them liquid
idea: Long take-or-pay contracts finance clusters but trap capacity and exclude startups as credit requirements spread; quotes are hard to compare, so RFQs, forward contracts and resale markets (backed by real clusters) are proposed.

title: Object-storage-native search with cached hot data fits AI economics
idea: Write to object storage, index in the background and cache the queried slice on SSD/memory, minimizing round trips, rather than keeping whole corpora in memory.

title: Keep history outside the window and retrieve it on demand each turn
idea: Instead of carrying the whole conversation, store the session externally and rebuild context per turn by retrieval, which handles topic switches and interruptions better than relying on what compaction kept.

title: Pre-index structure so agents navigate a domain without opening everything
idea: Precompute hierarchies, folder summaries or file indexes so the agent picks where to look, bounding per-query cost regardless of corpus size.

title: Encode the enterprise as a queryable ontology/knowledge graph shared by agents
idea: Business ontologies mapped to technical sources form a shared layer agents query, avoiding per-agent source discovery; one talk calls this the enterprise's moat.

title: Every memory fact must trace back to the episodes that produced it
idea: Set-valued, mutation-surviving lineage from facts to source episodes enables audit, debugging of bad memories and compliance deletion. Talks span graph memory, persistent agent memory and context-tier provenance records.

title: Separate conversation state from sandbox state via server-side IDs
idea: Server-held interaction IDs carry conversational context without resending history, while environment IDs let a fresh agent reuse an existing sandbox filesystem.

title: Evidence acquisition is the bottleneck: close the oracle gap with better retrieval
idea: Models answer well when handed evidence but poorly when they must find it; better search harnesses, searcher subagents, multimodal retrieval and RL training narrow the gap.

title: Embeddings are cached computation paid at index time
idea: Embedding is precomputed relevance work that makes query-time retrieval cheap and can augment agent grep exploration; indexes can be reused across users.

title: Answer identity/date/filter questions with structured queries, not vector RAG
idea: When correctness depends on identities, states and dates, translate the question into validated queries over a discovered schema with fuzzy identity resolution; embeddings cannot separate near-duplicate names.

title: Curate the corpus (dedupe, stale removal, metadata enrichment) before tuning retrieval
idea: Stale and duplicate documents crowd top-k; AI-assisted taxonomy, ontology-based metadata and structured attributes improve recall more than retriever changes.

title: Measure retrieval with a judgment set before adding stages like rerankers
idea: A small hand-built benchmark lets each retrieval change, including rerankers, be justified by measured precision gains.

title: Cross-framework agent messaging needs real transport primitives
