idea: Remote agent collaboration needs ordered delivery, retries, session continuity and identity that agent-as-tool calls and chat platforms lack; automating the human who routes messages between agents is the motivating case.

title: Design environments and incentives so agent collectives self-organize
idea: Fixed harnesses fit bounded work; open problems call for environments with information, incentives, verifiers and governance from which collective behavior emerges.

title: Dense, richer-than-scalar learning signals beat sparse rewards
idea: Token-level on-policy self-distillation and LLM reflection over full traces and textual feedback give denser credit assignment than scalar RLHF/GRPO rewards, avoiding reward-shaping regressions and improving sample efficiency.

title: Invest in data curation pipelines before scaling compute
idea: Better data steepens scaling laws: dedupe, quality-filter, resample to the task distribution, caption and tag at scale, and check coverage. Talks cover text reasoning data (OpenThoughts), pretraining mixes and billion-image datasets, often distilling a large model into a cheap filter.

title: Fine-tune tiny models for narrow on-device tasks and measure on the target hardware
idea: A tiny model fine-tuned (often on synthetic data) for one function-calling or agent task can go from unreliable to ~90% accurate on devices like a Raspberry Pi; quantization, runtime choice, small guardrail models and memory limits must be tuned on the actual device.

title: Measure audible response time from the user's last syllable, against human turn-taking norms
idea: Humans switch turns in ~200 ms; ~600 ms feels human and ~1.5 s is the edge of conversational. Dashboard latency misleads because TTS leading silence and first-sentence time dominate.

title: Open-weight TTS is now viable for real-time and on-device voice
idea: Small open TTS models run on CPU, reach sub-200 ms first-token latency and clone voices from short samples, removing cloud cost and latency.

title: Add voice as an interface layer over an agent's existing tools
idea: Keep the agent's orchestration, retrieval and tools, and add speech in/out around it; voice can trigger tools mid-conversation and need not always talk back (speech-to-action, event-to-speech).

title: Physical-world reliability: learned policies with failure-targeted data vs modular tool-based autonomy
idea: Demos are easy, reliability is hard. One approach fine-tunes generalist policies and uses reward models to target recovery data at failures; others keep modular edge/cloud autonomy and let LLM/VLM agents pick among existing robot tools. Both feed fleet data back into models.

title: Give coding agents concrete accessibility rules, since they copy inaccessible patterns
idea: Agents reproduce existing accessibility issues and ignore generic 'be accessible' advice; concrete rules or an accessibility skill (semantic HTML first, specific ARIA and keyboard behavior) plus audits and human testing fix generated UI. One talk reports cheaper, faster runs with keyboard-usable output.

title: Persona prompting does not faithfully simulate people; validate against real distributions
idea: Synthetic respondents and role-play personas fail through confounders, prompt sensitivity and cultural composites, and resampling one model is a single forecast. Remedies are temporally anchored preregistered tests and fine-tuning on real response distributions; preference tuning can make personas more pleasing but less faithful.

title: Formal methods replace probabilistic checks for agent-generated code
idea: Because LLM judges are probabilistic and tests cover only some inputs, use formal verification (Lean proofs, SMT equivalence checks) so humans validate specs while agents generate implementations and proofs; SMT can also surface spec ambiguity.

title: Generate tool schemas and client bindings from code so specs cannot drift
idea: Derive tool definitions from typed function signatures and ship version-pinned bindings with the harness, so interfaces never drift from implementations.

title: Skills can replace product feature code, at a cost
idea: Markdown skills plus slash commands replaced thousands of lines of feature code and are pitched as the new product features, but cost isolation, discoverability and consistency versus code-enforced features.

title: Strong model plans and reviews; a cheap fast model implements
idea: Pair a larger planning/review model with a faster cheaper execution model, steering actively instead of one-shot prompts.

title: Agents delegating implementation breaks the junior training path
idea: If juniors no longer do implementation tickets they lose the reps that build judgment, so leaders must deliberately teach discovery, spec writing and product judgment, and juniors must seek feedback on purpose.

title: Treat early design-partner pilots as discovery, then scale through self-service
idea: Early large design partnerships are hands-on discovery of what the platform must become, distinct from the scalable motion; build the self-service sales machine before adding people and limit resource-heavy pilots.

title: Agent-generated contributions overload open-source maintainers
idea: AI-generated PRs, issues and reports burden maintainers, prompting bans, policies and auto-close defenses that demand a human voice.

title: Cheaper software makes previously uneconomic software worth building
idea: As agents shrink build cost, nice-to-have software and former startups become viable side projects, pushing build over buy and rethinking project scale.

title: Price AI products as a subscription base plus usage credits
idea: Hybrid pricing protects margins from variable inference cost while billing in customer-perceived units with spend visibility and prepaid credits.

title: Keep the model and the rendered UI in sync
idea: Anything a widget shows must also reach the model as data, user interactions must be reported back, and search should be separate from rendering so the model can reason before displaying; private data can be selectively withheld.

title: Interaction design, not model capability, limits AI's value
idea: Models advanced while interaction stayed a batch punch-card protocol, leaving a capability overhang that product experience must unlock for non-engineers.

title: Discover preferences by reacting to generated options, not upfront articulation
idea: Users often cannot state what they want; run a discovery phase, show options visually and use fast generation to shape preferences through making.

title: Be candid with users about limitations and what to verify
idea: State what works, what must be verified and what is out of scope; honesty builds more trust than overclaiming.

title: Inspect model internals (activations, KV cache) to catch what text filters and evals miss
idea: Behavioral evals and prompt classifiers cannot see backdoors firing on untested cues or injections hidden in audio; diff-based sparse autoencoders on activations and learned baselines over KV pages give computation-level signals without per-attack classifiers.

title: Make sign-up and API access agent-native via a discoverable auth.md
idea: Human signup flows (forms, CAPTCHA, manual keys) break agent workflows; publish an auth.md declaring registration, scopes and limits, let anonymous agents try limited actions, then have the user claim the work to issue a delegated token. The app, not the file, enforces authorization.

title: Render untrusted generated UI in origin-isolated sandbox iframes; never relax host CSP
idea: Generated or third-party UI runs in null-origin or separate-origin sandbox iframes talking via postMessage RPC; srcdoc iframes inherit parent CSP, so relaxing CSP or injecting nonces to make apps work opens real holes.

title: Verify dependencies: models hallucinate package names that attackers register (slopsquatting)
idea: Attackers publish backdoored packages under names models invent, so check dependency provenance before installing.

title: Harden the software supply chain: cooldowns, signing, provenance and side doors
idea: Compromises propagate through shared dependencies and tooling (CI/CD, workstations, agent tooling, malicious MCP packages after clean releases); defenses include package cooldowns, Sigstore/SLSA provenance and security keys.

title: Grade security agents with the program as oracle, not an LLM judge
idea: For security RL and benchmarks, use deterministic outcomes (crash, exploit success, access-control checks); reward hacking is a major risk and novel vulns lack ground truth. Broken access control needs whole-system reasoning.

title: Red-team agent policies continuously against adversarial input variations
idea: Attack surface grows with capability; test constraints against jailbreaks and input variations continuously (borrowing from robustness testing), not once before launch.

title: Engine internals decide utilization: batching, paged KV, chunked prefill, CUDA graphs, scheduler
idea: Decode keeps up via continuous batching, paged KV allocation, prefix reuse and chunked prefill; CUDA graphs cut launch overhead, and the CPU scheduler can bottleneck the GPU despite doing little compute.

title: Speculative decoding helps only with compatible drafters, high acceptance and small batches
idea: Gains appear with spare VRAM, small batches and predictable output; a mismatched drafter can cut speed 3x, high temperature erodes acceptance, and it speeds decode not prefill. Check acceptance rate and draft memory cost before enabling.

title: Stack quantization, caching and step distillation to make diffusion near real-time
idea: Diffusion image/video generation becomes real-time by combining quantization, chunk-level caching of unchanged regions and step distillation rather than 20-50 denoising steps.

title: Cost per token is set by operator capability: compare by usable output per dollar
idea: The same GPUs give very different output depending on the serving stack, so compare producers by total spend over quality-constrained output, not rental price; per-token price drops can still raise bills when upgrades emit more tokens.

title: Choose the production model on the accuracy versus latency tradeoff
idea: The most accurate model or largest prompt is often too slow for interactive use; trade accuracy against latency explicitly.

title: System-shared on-device model vs bundling your own: managed vs controllable
idea: A system model shared via AICore avoids downloads and memory duplication, while shipping your own via LiteRT gives custom models at maintenance cost.

title: Keep the edge device thin; do heavy work and output shaping server-side
idea: Run cheap hackable devices with cloud inference, and shape output (strip markdown, cap length, paginate) in the backend so firmware only renders fixed buffers.

title: GPU utilization numbers mislead; profile the real bottleneck at each scale
idea: Utilization % hides data-loading starvation, networking and throttling; async fetching, object references and prefetch fixed GPU starvation, and bottlenecks shift (e.g., NIC saturation) as scale grows, so re-profile each stage.

title: Skip the Docker build-push loop by running local code directly on remote GPUs
idea: Decorating functions or attaching local code to live cloud GPUs with on-the-fly dependencies removes ~15-minute build/registry/provision iterations.

title: Verify data migrations and recovery by row counts and convergence, not logs
idea: Backup/restore or CDC logs don't prove correctness; compare row counts, attributes and replica convergence, with idempotent consumers.

title: Data sovereignty needs explicit control over where data is processed and by whom
idea: Cross-border processing and provider dependence break first; split application, control and data planes so customers keep data in their own infrastructure while the vendor operates the agent.

title: Data agents need a curated semantic layer of metric definitions
idea: The same metric means different things per team, so bigger models give confident wrong answers; authoritative KPI definitions, lineage and grain must be captured (deterministically where possible) with feedback loops. Per-user preference routing between valid definitions is unresolved.

title: Cross-silo agent collaboration is a shared-knowledge problem, not live agent chat
idea: Getting the right information across organizational silos into context matters more than agents querying each other; AI-maintained shared knowledge with disclosure policies avoids conflicting answers between disconnected agents.

title: Precompute a user world model offline instead of retrieving disconnected items
idea: Answering 'what should I focus on' needs relationships across email, tasks, calendar and CRM precomputed offline into a model the assistant reads, with fallback to last verified context.

title: Consumer memory moved to background-updated profiles, with staleness and visibility risks
idea: Assistants evolved from injected saved-fact lists to dense running profiles; benefits are faster understanding, failure modes are stale or wrongly inferred memories users cannot see.

title: Enforce permissions and tenant isolation inside the index and storage layer
idea: Post- or pre-filtering vectors by permission fails; native permission-aware indexes and per-tenant namespaces keep latency low and satisfy isolation.

title: Define an RL environment once and reuse it for evals, RL, SFT and distillation
idea: An environment is a package of tasks, harness/interaction rules and a verifier/reward; built once, it scores models and produces training signal, so post-training becomes an iterate loop of build, score, read rollouts, train, deploy.

title: Curriculum and difficulty design shape what RL learns
idea: Task difficulty (opponent strength, progressively harder exploit targets) and reward design determine whether RL learns; build a graded, reproducible curriculum and watch for instability from batch size and temperature.

title: Rewards without ground truth (LLM judges, human preference) are needed but fragile
idea: Most real agent tasks have no golden answer, so rewards come from judges, rubrics or rater preference; these invite reward hacking and optimize for what pleases raters (chatty assistants) rather than reliable action. Task difficulty must be calibrated to keep such rewards informative.

title: Synthetic data: complement to organic data or a threat to diversity
idea: One view: synthetic rephrasing regularizes presentation, fills under-represented formats and beats seeds-only training, while hard quality filters backfire through repetition. The opposing view avoids synthetic training images to preserve unconventional styles and aesthetic diversity.

title: Continual learning is a design space: pick the layer and data regime per failure
idea: Agents can be improved in weights, harness or memory, from offline or on-policy data, via SFT, RL, LoRA or prompt optimization. Talks propose axes (replayability, lifelongness, efficiency; hints vs traces) for picking per failure, with regression-gated replayable environments.

title: Train text and vision together from the first step
idea: Bolting vision onto a pretrained text model degrades text ability or is fragile; joint multimodal training from scratch nearly preserves text performance.

title: LLM recommenders over semantic item IDs
idea: Represent catalog items as semantic IDs so an LLM natively generates recommendations, training on language plus catalog data in stages that keep language steerability.

title: Voice-captured data is structured extraction: schema up front, confirm before sync
idea: Treat call data like a typed form with field-level evaluation; LLM summarization and extraction cut after-call work, with PII masked early, channels kept separate, and operator confirmation before CRM sync.

title: Direct synthetic voices with natural-language descriptions
idea: Prompt TTS for style, emotion and accent, or generate a character voice from a text description of era, culture and personality.

title: Don't trust generic ASR transcripts: domain-tune or clean them before acting
idea: Generic ASR fails on domain terms like drug names; fine-tune it or clean unreliable transcripts before the agent acts.
